verdict: CenterPoint grew revenue 10% to $2.2B and earned $331M as Houston's electric demand and rate recovery lifted its electric business — and it raised guidance while expanding its 10-year building plan to $70.7B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $2.2B in revenue, vs $2.0B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.45 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $0.53

kpis.label: 10-year capital plan
kpis.note: Raised by $4.0B to build capacity for Greater Houston growth

segments.name: Electric
segments.note: Delivering electricity — transmission, distribution and generation, mainly Houston (Houston Electric) and Indiana. Growth and rate recovery drove the rise.

segments.name: Natural gas
segments.note: Gas distribution to homes and businesses in Texas, Minnesota, Indiana and other states.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small corporate and other revenue, net of eliminations.

opex.name: Operations & maintenance
opex.note: Running and maintaining the wires, pipes and plants day to day — flat versus a year ago relative to growth.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of the grid and pipelines over their long useful lives — it rises as the company builds more.

follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.

takeaways.title: Electric is the growth story
takeaways.text: Electric revenue rose 13% to $1,549M. Growth and rate recovery added $0.09 a share versus a year ago and weather and usage added $0.03, partly offset by $0.04 of higher financing costs. Gas revenue rose 3% to $640M.

takeaways.title: A bigger building plan
takeaways.text: CenterPoint raised its 10-year capital plan by $4.0B to $70.7B and pulled $1.5B of spending into 2026–2030, supporting rate-base growth of more than 14% a year through 2030 — and it sees at least $10B more of possible projects through 2035 as Houston demand accelerates.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised, 2027 started higher
takeaways.text: Full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance rose to $1.90–$1.92, and 2027 guidance was initiated at $2.07–$2.09 — about 9% growth at the midpoint each year. The company extended its 7%–9% annual growth outlook through 2030.

oneTimers: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.53 excludes items GAAP counts: a $19M cost from temporary emergency electric energy facilities removed from rate base, $19M of mark-to-market loss on indexed debt securities (partly offset by a $17M gain on equity securities) and $2M of merger and divestiture impacts — non-GAAP income was $354M versus $331M GAAP. The sale of the Ohio natural gas business closed on October 1, 2026, just after the quarter ended.
otherDetail: Other expense of $254M, net: $259M of interest expense and $22M of interest on securitization bonds, partly offset by $30M of other income, a $21M gain on equity securities, and a $24M loss on indexed debt securities.
footerNote: For a utility, the direct cost of revenue is the fuel, purchased power and natural gas the company buys to serve customers ($187M utility plus $1M non-utility).
